title: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on major Saudi oil refinery
summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Wednesday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the kingdom's largest, which is near a major export terminal for Saudi crude.

image.caption: A satellite image shows a large smoke cloud billowing over Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery after Yemen's Houthi military leadership said in a statement that they attacked the industrial facility on Wednesday. (NASA Worldview/Reuters)

blocks.text: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Wednesday they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the kingdom's largest, which is near a major export terminal for Saudi crude.
Satellite imagery shows thick smoke over Ras Tanura site, near major export terminal
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the refinery attack caused fires.

The Houthi militia, which controls much of western Yemen including the capital Sanaa, has been firing at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July in a spillover from the U.S.-Iran war.

The attacks have previously temporarily disrupted some operations of Aramco, the state oil giant, and caused the cancellation of most international flights to Riyadh. They also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including soccer's AFC Asian Cup and flagship investment conference FII.

The Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Wednesday that air defences had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. It did not say the refinery there had been struck.
NASA satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters showed large swathes of thick black smoke around the refinery, covering an area of around 600 square kilometres.
The Saudi government communications office and Aramco did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
How the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict plays into broader Middle East war
Ras Tanura, which has a refining capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, has previously been targeted during the conflict with the Houthis as well as during the broader Iran war.

It is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast that was the kingdom's main export terminal until the U.S.-Iran war boosted the importance of Yanbu on the west coast, which receives oil via the East-West pipeline.
Saree, the Houthi spokesman, also said the group had attacked Riyadh's financial district.

blocks.text: Saudi civil defence confirmed 11 people were wounded on Tuesday in a strike on a tower in the capital, the tallest building in the city that houses the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund. It was the second strike on the tower in less than a week.

The first, on Thursday, damaged the building but caused no injuries. The Saudi civil defence posted an image on Tuesday of the landmark tower showing some damage to the building about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact from last week's attack.
The Houthis have attacked Saudi energy facilities and airports in recent weeks, saying they aim to pressure the kingdom into lifting its blockade on Yemen.

Separately, the Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia for a strike that killed eight people from the same family, including women and children, on Tuesday. The Associated Press could not independently verify the claim. The Houthi-run Health Ministry said the attack was on Lahj, a province where displaced families have fled since fighting resumed.
With files from The Associated Press
